extracted.intended_audience: interested parties in antidumping administrative reviews (exporters, importers, petitioners, counsel, and other trade stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for participating in an antidumping duty administrative review before the U.S. Department of Commerce, including grounds for rescission, submission and formatting of comments/briefs, hearing requests, assessment and cash-deposit rules, and timelines. The notice applies to the administrative review for aluminum extrusions from China but mostly cites general regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of administrative review (19 CFR 351.213(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce will rescind an administrative review, in whole or in part, if the party or parties that requested a review withdraw the request within 90 days of the publication date of the notice of initiation of the requested review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied here: all requests for review were timely withdrawn for 79 of the 97 companies named in the Initiation Notice; Commerce is rescinding the review with respect to those 79 companies (see Appendix II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate rate eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties seeking a separate rate must submit evidence demonstrating eligibility for separate rate status; failure to submit such evidence results in being treated as part of the China-wide entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of the 18 companies for which review was requested and not withdrawn, none submitted evidence of eligibility for separate rate status; Commerce preliminarily determined those companies are not eligible and are part of the China-wide entity (see Appendix III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional review of China-wide entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Commerce's policy, the China-wide entity will not be under review unless a party specifically requests a review, or Commerce self-initiates a review of the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no party requested a review of the China-wide entity in this review, and Commerce did not self-initiate, the entity is not under review and its current China-wide rate (86.01 percent) is not subject to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of calculations (19 CFR 351.224(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce ordinarily discloses to interested parties the calculations performed in connection with the preliminary results within five days of the public announcement or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Commerce did not calculate weighted-average dumping margins (as in this instance), there is nothing to disclose; making such a disclosure (or noting absence) satisfies the regulatory obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case brief submission deadline and format (19 CFR 351.309(c)(1)(ii) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case briefs or other written comments may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary; deadline modified here to no later than 21 days after the date of publication of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties who submit case briefs must include: (1) a table of contents listing each issue; and (2) a table of authorities. Commerce requests a public executive summary (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief timing and scope (19 CFR 351.309(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing case briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttal briefs must be limited to replying to issues raised in case briefs; procedural rules (service/APO) may also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public executive summary requirement and limits (19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)(iii) and (d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties should provide at the beginning of their briefs a public, executive summary for each issue raised in the briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce requests that the public executive summary of each issue be limited to no more than 450 words (not including citations) and that parties include footnotes for relevant citations. Commerce intends to use these public executive summaries as the basis for comment summaries in the Issues and Decision Memorandum accompanying the final results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request requirements and limits (19 CFR 351.310(c)/(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties who wish to request a hearing (limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs) must submit a written request via ACCESS by 5:00 p.m. ET within 30 days after publication of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of issues to be discussed. Oral presentations at the hearing will be limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs. If a hearing is requested, parties will be notified of date/time/location and should confirm the date, time, and location two days before the scheduled hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instructions to CBP and timing (section 751(a)(2)(C) and 19 CFR 351.212(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of the final results, Commerce shall determine, and CBP shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by the review. For rescinded companies, CBP should assess at rates equal to the cash deposit required at time of entry during the POR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce intends to issue rescission/assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after publication of the notice. For individually calculated respondents and non-selected separate rate respondents, Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions no earlier than 35 days after publication of the final results. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (i.e., within 90 days of publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final results deadline (section 751(a)(3)(A) and 19 CFR 351.213(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue the final results of the administrative review, including analysis of issues raised in case and rebuttal briefs, within 120 days of these preliminary results, unless the deadline is extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 120-day run time begins from the preliminary results publication and is subject to statutory/regulatory extensions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit requirements upon publication of final results (section 751(a)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash deposit requirements will be effective upon publication of the final results of the administrative review for shipments entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four categories: (1) for individually calculated respondent and non-selected separate rate respondents, the cash deposit rate will equal the weighted-average dumping margin established in the final results (except if de minimis, then deposit = 0); (2) for any previously investigated or reviewed Chinese and non-Chinese exporters that received a separate rate in a prior segment, the deposit rate will continue to be the existing exporter-specific rate; (3) for all Chinese exporters not found entitled to a separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the China-wide entity rate (86.01% here); (4) for non-Chinese exporters without their own rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable to the Chinese exporter that supplied that non-Chinese exporter. These deposit requirements remain in effect until further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer reimbursement certificate requirement (19 CFR 351.402(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Importers are responsible for filing a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during the POR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties and/or an increase in the amount of antidumping duties by the amount of countervailing duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief contents: table of contents and table of authorities (19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)/(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties submitting case or rebuttal briefs must include a table of contents listing each issue and a table of authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formatting and organizational requirements support Commerce's review and preparation of Issues and Decision Memoranda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Preliminary Decision Memorandum and scope reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preliminary Decision Memorandum contains a complete description of events, scope, methodology, and topics addressed in the preliminary results and is a public document available via ACCESS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the complete description of the scope of the Order and the methodology used, parties are directed to the Preliminary Decision Memorandum (topics listed in Appendix I). The scope of this Order is 'aluminum extrusions from China'—parties should consult the memorandum for the full scope description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling of deadlines due to lapse in appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines in administrative proceedings may be tolled during a lapse in appropriations or other events as memorialized in Commerce memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, Commerce tolled deadlines by 47 days (memo dated Nov 14, 2025) and an additional 21 days (memo dated Nov 24, 2025) due to a government shutdown and backlog, which affected the preliminary results deadline (moved to April 9, 2026). Parties should account for tolling memos when calculating deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public filing channels and document access (ACCESS, Federal Register, govinfo.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key documents (e.g., Preliminary Decision Memorandum, briefs, public inspection version) are available electronically via ACCESS for registered users and the official PDF on govinfo.gov; FederalRegister.gov provides an XML rendition that is informational but not the official legal edition until ACFR grants it legal status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should verify contents against official editions where legal notice is required. ACCESS links and the public inspection PDF are provided for document retrieval.
